bull_bear.body: Prioritizing internal accruals and debt for Rajasthan rollout; no dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on ROCE improvement toward 15%+
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Govt payment delays (SNA-SPARSH system issues); receivables cycle extension (150 days); operational disruption from natural disasters (e.g., Punjab/Himachal floods); retail breakeven delayed beyond initial expectations
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, mission-driven, emphasizing scale, quality, and social impact; optimistic on retail and Rajasthan rollout; transparent on working capital issues but dismissive of long-term risk
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Krsnaa’s 36 NABH + 57 NABL + CAP + ACR accreditations create an unmatched quality moat in public diagnostics; retail growth is being funded by PPP cash flows, not equity; senior citizen access is already embedded via PPP, not a separate initiative
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Strategic framing is 'Reach -> Capacity -> Trust -> Cash Conversion', with management explicitly naming the 'next phase' as cash growth / building a larger, more sustainable cash business.
- PPP infrastructure (existing CT/MRI/pathology assets) is leveraged for retail at marginal revenue and minimal incremental fixed cost, framed as delivering superior ROCE.
- Asset-light franchise model - partnerships with local operators, franchise arrangements and collection-centre networks - used to fund expansion without heavy capital outlays.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- scale: multi-state PPP diagnostics network spanning radiology and pathology — evidence: 190 CT/MRI centres, 147 pathology laboratories and more than 4,700 patient collection centres; presence across 331 districts — against it: a significant portion of operations is linked to PPP projects and government tenders, making contract renewals and policy continuity important
- technology: centralised tele-radiology reporting that extends radiology into areas short of radiologists — evidence: NABH-accredited tele-radiology hub in Pune provides round-the-clock remote reporting across the CT/MRI network; company states it is the first company outside the US to receive ACR accreditation
- cost position: shared infrastructure between PPP and retail — evidence: pathology common processing units and radiology common imaging centres serve both PPP and retail; retail business scaled on existing PPP infrastructure under an asset-light model
- customer lock-in: long-term exclusive diagnostics partnership with Apulki's hospital network — evidence: Krsnaa to serve as Apulki's exclusive diagnostics partner with PET-CT diagnostics centres, for an initial term of 30 years with a renewal option for a further 30 years [planned]
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on government / PPP contracts — A significant portion of the business comes from government and PPP contracts; delays in tender awards, payment cycles, policy changes or budgetary constraints may affect revenues, cash flows and working capital, and contract renewals and policy continuity matter for growth.
- Temporary suspension of PPP centres — Suspension or delay of operations at PPP diagnostic centres for administrative, contractual or regulatory reasons may reduce patient volumes and revenue growth.
- Input cost escalation under long-term PPP contracts — Geopolitical conflicts may raise the cost of imported diagnostic equipment, reagents and consumables, pressuring margins particularly under long-term PPP contracts.
- Competition and low retail entry barriers — Organised chains, regional operators and hospital-based labs may pressure pricing, margins and share across PPP and retail; relatively low entry barriers in retail diagnostics let new regional players enter.
- Specialist talent availability — Attracting and retaining qualified radiologists, pathologists and technicians is critical to operational efficiency, service quality and expansion plans.
- Technology obsolescence — Rapid advances in diagnostic and imaging equipment may require continuous upgrades and capital investment to stay competitive.
- Regulatory and accreditation changes — Changes in healthcare regulation, accreditation requirements, clinical standards, pricing regulation or taxation may raise compliance costs and affect operations.
- Cybersecurity and patient-data privacy — Growing digitisation of health records and diagnostic services exposes the company to cyberattacks, data breaches and unauthorised access to sensitive patient information.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Radiology: 200+ CT/MRI centers (largest fleet in Asia); Pathology: 57 NABL labs; Retail: 60% QoQ growth, 8% of H1 revenue, targeting 15-20% in FY27; PPP: 18 states covered, 36 NABH radiology centers, India’s first CAP pathology lab in govt facility
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- One of India's largest integrated diagnostic service providers spanning radiology, pathology and tele-radiology, built around the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model for affordable, accessible care.
- One of India's largest NABH-accredited tele-radiology reporting hubs, with capability to process X-rays, CT and MRI scans in real time for patients at the remotest locations.
- Accreditation leader with 120 total NABL+NABH accreditations (66 NABH, 54 NABL) - 2.3x the next-largest tracked peer (Peer A at 53; others range 7-44).
- First-mover credentials: India's 1st ACR-accredited company, 1st NABH-accredited tele-radiology hub, and 1st CAP-accredited lab at a government facility.
- Well-diversified regional revenue mix in Q1 FY27: North 40%, West 39%, South 11%, East 10%.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Policy tailwinds] Deck cites sector tailwinds: India's healthcare spend as a share of GDP seen rising from 3.3% to 5% by 2030; MoHFW Budget of Rs 1,017 Bn (Union Budget 2025-26); PM-ABHIM outlay of Rs 42 Bn (FY2025-26); Indian healthcare industry estimated at $1,522 Bn by FY29-30; and a diagnostics TAM of Rs 2.98 Tn by FY30.
- [Contract structure] Long-tenure PPP contracts (radiology ~10+ years, pathology ~5+ years) with a captive government OPD/IPD patient base across district, subdistrict, community and primary healthcare centres.
- [Radiology disruption] The radiology platform continues to expand despite the discontinuation of the Tamil Nadu MRI contract.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Krsnaa Diagnostics runs radiology (MRI, CT, X-ray and other imaging), pathology (hub-and-spoke laboratory testing) and tele-radiology reporting services, delivered mainly through PPP contracts with government hospitals and healthcare institutions across multiple Indian states. It is also building an asset-light retail diagnostics business under the RPL brand that reuses its PPP infrastructure, offering pathology and radiology tests, preventive health packages and home sample collection to consumers, with a focus on Tier II, Tier III and underserved regions.

business.body:

- **Pathology:** Biochemistry, Haematology, Microbiology, Histopathology, Cytopathology, Serology, Immunology, Molecular diagnostics
- **Tele-radiology:** NABH-accredited tele-radiology reporting hub (Pune) with round-the-clock remote reporting for CT and MRI centres
- **Retail diagnostics (RPL brand):** Pathology and radiology tests, Preventive healthcare / wellness packages, Specialised diagnostics testing, Home sample collection, Online booking and app-based services

outlook.body: revenue growth: higher teens YoY in FY27; margin: sustained 29%+ EBITDA margin; order inflow: pipeline active but undisclosed; capex/commissioning: Rajasthan PPP full rollout by end-Q4FY26, no new equity raise planned
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rajasthan PPP: 10 labs operational by Nov 2025; 25 labs + 500 collection centers by Dec 2025; 152 labs + 1,100 collection centers by end-Q4FY26
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Retail to contribute 40-50% of revenue in 5 years; expansion into wellness/preventive diagnostics; AI-driven reporting and home collection scaling; potential for national PPP tender wins
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Execute large PPP diagnostic projects in underserved regions, led by the Rajasthan diagnostic project connecting smaller towns and remote districts to organised diagnostics.
- Build retail diagnostics as a second engine alongside PPP, so that PPP provides reach and scale while retail takes the Krsnaa relationship directly to the consumer.
- Scale retail on the diagnostic infrastructure already built for PPP, limiting additional capital and customer acquisition costs; expand through local operators, franchises and collection-centre networks rather than heavy capital outlay.
- Expand the MRI and advanced imaging footprint with a focus on Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
- Run pathology on a hub-and-spoke architecture of centralised reference labs processing samples from a wider satellite network to keep quality consistent and costs low at scale.
- Grow B2C wellness through the AYAKSHAM wellness brand and a retail website soft-launched in Mumbai and Pune, with bundled test packages priced for accessibility.
- Build home collection around a phlebotomist network and a digital platform for booking, real-time tracking and report delivery.
- Hold three constants stated by the Chairman: affordability, quality, and taking diagnostics to places where access remains inadequate.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion is network build-out rather than plant capacity. The largest project is the Rajasthan State Pathology Project, one of the largest pathology infrastructure projects in the country, being implemented on a hub-and-spoke model across all districts of Rajasthan; it has entered the implementation phase with 27 mother labs and more than 800 collection centres being rolled out. In FY2025 the company secured contracts in Maharashtra, Assam, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand for new radiology centres, pathology laboratories and collection centres, and during FY26 commissioned new CT and MRI centres in states including Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, operationalising 51 centres and over 1,100 collection centres. Management indicated the existing order book will take the radiology network beyond 200 CT/MRI centres while significantly expanding pathology in Rajasthan. The Asian Development Bank sanctioned a Rs 430 crore long-term credit facility to support Rajasthan and other PPP projects under implementation, and the MD&A notes higher borrowings and capital expenditure reflect this ongoing expansion. Retail diagnostics is being expanded on an asset-light model that reuses PPP infrastructure; retail touchpoints rose from 1,673 in FY2025 to 3,500 in FY2026, including over 500 franchises and collection centres across five states.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Rising preventive-healthcare awareness and increasing diagnostic penetration in India.
- Governments recognising the role of public-private partnerships in expanding healthcare capacity; of the 12 states and Union Territories that have adopted the PPP model for pathology, the company has won tenders in eight.
- A 75% win-to-bid ratio in government tenders positions the company to capture further radiology centres under PPP models.
- Radiology is described as the higher-margin part of the business mix, with test volumes drawn from a captive patient base through hospital referrals and GP-referred walk-ins, which reduces the seasonal fluctuations typical of pathology.
- Technology and artificial intelligence allowing specialist expertise to reach beyond a doctor's physical location.
- Consumers increasingly expecting healthcare that is more accessible, transparent and convenient, supporting retail and home collection.
- Industry-level: diagnostics is among the fastest-growing healthcare segments, helped by preventive care, early detection, chronic disease management and government programmes such as Ayushman Bharat, PM-JAY and PM-ABHIM.
- On completion of the current order book, the radiology network will comprise 200+ CT/MRI centres (190 centres at FY26).
- On completion of the Rajasthan project, the pathology network will expand to 7 Reference Labs, 41 Mother Labs, 249 Satellite Labs and 5,000+ Collection Centres.
- Radiology has averaged 20+ centres added each year over the past five years through tender wins.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Krsnaa delivered 11% YoY revenue growth and 29% EBITDA margin despite PPP contract transitions, driven by retail scaling and operational efficiencies; the imminent Rajasthan PPP rollout by Dec 2025 is the key catalyst for FY27 revenue acceleration and margin uplift.

It is also building an asset-light retail diagnostics business under the RPL brand that reuses its PPP infrastructure, offering pathology and radiology tests, preventive health packages and home sample collection to consumers, with a focus on Tier II, Tier III and underserved regions.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- KDPL Diagnostics (Amritsar) Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary (100%); pays revenue-share income to the Company
- KDPL Diagnostics (Bathinda) Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary (100%); pays revenue-share income to the Company
- KDPL Diagnostics (Jalandhar) Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary (100%); pays revenue-share income to the Company
- KDPL Diagnostics (Ludhiana) Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary (100%); pays revenue-share income to the Company
- KDPL Diagnostics (Patiala) Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary (100%); pays revenue-share income to the Company
- KDPL Diagnostics (SAS Nagar) Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary (100%); pays revenue-share income to the Company
- Krsnaa Diagnostics (Mohali) Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary (100%); pays revenue-share income to the Company
- Krsnaa Retail Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary (100%); holds the 26% stake in Apulki Healthcare (KDMC) Private Limited; has received a loan from and pays revenue-share income to the Company
- Apulki Healthcare (KDMC) Private Limited — associate: Step-down associate: 26% held through wholly-owned subsidiary Krsnaa Retail Private Limited (which acquired an additional 16% in FY26); the Company holds no shares directly
- Apulki Healthcare Private Limited — related party: Was an associate (up to March 26, 2026) and an entity under common control (up to April 02, 2026); ceased to be an associate of the Company during the year; the Company had invested in its equity
- Krsna International Limited-Yemen — related party: Entity under common control
- Krsna Diagnostics (Mumbai) Private Limited — related party: Entity in which KMP exercise significant influence
- Ms. Sunita Mutha — related party: Relative of KMP; the Company pays her rent

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Radiology: 200+ CT/MRI centers (largest fleet in Asia); Pathology: 57 NABL labs; Retail: 60% QoQ growth, 8% of H1 revenue, targeting 15-20% in FY27; PPP: 18 states covered, 36 NABH radiology centers, India’s first CAP pathology lab in govt facility

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Radiology:** MRI, CT scans, X-rays, Mammography, Ultrasound, Colour Doppler, Bone densitometry
- **Pathology:** Biochemistry, Haematology, Microbiology, Histopathology, Cytopathology, Serology, Immunology, Molecular diagnostics
- **Tele-radiology:** NABH-accredited tele-radiology reporting hub (Pune) with round-the-clock remote reporting for CT and MRI centres
- **Retail diagnostics (RPL brand):** Pathology and radiology tests, Preventive healthcare / wellness packages, Specialised diagnostics testing, Home sample collection, Online booking and app-based services

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Retail to contribute 40-50% of revenue in 5 years; expansion into wellness/preventive diagnostics; AI-driven reporting and home collection scaling; potential for national PPP tender wins

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Rising preventive-healthcare awareness and increasing diagnostic penetration in India.
- Governments recognising the role of public-private partnerships in expanding healthcare capacity; of the 12 states and Union Territories that have adopted the PPP model for pathology, the company has won tenders in eight.
- A 75% win-to-bid ratio in government tenders positions the company to capture further radiology centres under PPP models.
- Radiology is described as the higher-margin part of the business mix, with test volumes drawn from a captive patient base through hospital referrals and GP-referred walk-ins, which reduces the seasonal fluctuations typical of pathology.
- Technology and artificial intelligence allowing specialist expertise to reach beyond a doctor's physical location.
- Consumers increasingly expecting healthcare that is more accessible, transparent and convenient, supporting retail and home collection.
- Industry-level: diagnostics is among the fastest-growing healthcare segments, helped by preventive care, early detection, chronic disease management and government programmes such as Ayushman Bharat, PM-JAY and PM-ABHIM.
- On completion of the current order book, the radiology network will comprise 200+ CT/MRI centres (190 centres at FY26).
- On completion of the Rajasthan project, the pathology network will expand to 7 Reference Labs, 41 Mother Labs, 249 Satellite Labs and 5,000+ Collection Centres.
- Radiology has averaged 20+ centres added each year over the past five years through tender wins.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin expanded to 29% via labor productivity, radiology utilization optimization, supply chain efficiency, and automation; retail still loss-making but breakeven expected at ~Rs.100cr revenue

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing internal accruals and debt for Rajasthan rollout; no dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on ROCE improvement toward 15%+

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Expansion is network build-out rather than plant capacity. The largest project is the Rajasthan State Pathology Project, one of the largest pathology infrastructure projects in the country, being implemented on a hub-and-spoke model across all districts of Rajasthan; it has entered the implementation phase with 27 mother labs and more than 800 collection centres being rolled out. In FY2025 the company secured contracts in Maharashtra, Assam, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand for new radiology centres, pathology laboratories and collection centres, and during FY26 commissioned new CT and MRI centres in states including Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, operationalising 51 centres and over 1,100 collection centres. Management indicated the existing order book will take the radiology network beyond 200 CT/MRI centres while significantly expanding pathology in Rajasthan. The Asian Development Bank sanctioned a Rs 430 crore long-term credit facility to support Rajasthan and other PPP projects under implementation, and the MD&A notes higher borrowings and capital expenditure reflect this ongoing expansion. Retail diagnostics is being expanded on an asset-light model that reuses PPP infrastructure; retail touchpoints rose from 1,673 in FY2025 to 3,500 in FY2026, including over 500 franchises and collection centres across five states.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, mission-driven, emphasizing scale, quality, and social impact; optimistic on retail and Rajasthan rollout; transparent on working capital issues but dismissive of long-term risk

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- scale: multi-state PPP diagnostics network spanning radiology and pathology — evidence: 190 CT/MRI centres, 147 pathology laboratories and more than 4,700 patient collection centres; presence across 331 districts — against it: a significant portion of operations is linked to PPP projects and government tenders, making contract renewals and policy continuity important
- technology: centralised tele-radiology reporting that extends radiology into areas short of radiologists — evidence: NABH-accredited tele-radiology hub in Pune provides round-the-clock remote reporting across the CT/MRI network; company states it is the first company outside the US to receive ACR accreditation
- cost position: shared infrastructure between PPP and retail — evidence: pathology common processing units and radiology common imaging centres serve both PPP and retail; retail business scaled on existing PPP infrastructure under an asset-light model
- customer lock-in: long-term exclusive diagnostics partnership with Apulki's hospital network — evidence: Krsnaa to serve as Apulki's exclusive diagnostics partner with PET-CT diagnostics centres, for an initial term of 30 years with a renewal option for a further 30 years [planned]

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Govt payment delays (SNA-SPARSH system issues); receivables cycle extension (150 days); operational disruption from natural disasters (e.g., Punjab/Himachal floods); retail breakeven delayed beyond initial expectations

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Krsnaa’s 36 NABH + 57 NABL + CAP + ACR accreditations create an unmatched quality moat in public diagnostics; retail growth is being funded by PPP cash flows, not equity; senior citizen access is already embedded via PPP, not a separate initiative

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Execute large PPP diagnostic projects in underserved regions, led by the Rajasthan diagnostic project connecting smaller towns and remote districts to organised diagnostics.
- Build retail diagnostics as a second engine alongside PPP, so that PPP provides reach and scale while retail takes the Krsnaa relationship directly to the consumer.
- Scale retail on the diagnostic infrastructure already built for PPP, limiting additional capital and customer acquisition costs; expand through local operators, franchises and collection-centre networks rather than heavy capital outlay.
- Expand the MRI and …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Policy tailwinds] Deck cites sector tailwinds: India's healthcare spend as a share of GDP seen rising from 3.3% to 5% by 2030; MoHFW Budget of Rs 1,017 Bn (Union Budget 2025-26); PM-ABHIM outlay of Rs 42 Bn (FY2025-26); Indian healthcare industry estimated at $1,522 Bn by FY29-30; and a diagnostics TAM of Rs 2.98 Tn by FY30.
- [Contract structure] Long-tenure PPP contracts (radiology ~10+ years, pathology ~5+ years) with a captive government OPD/IPD patient base across district, subdistrict, community and primary healthcare centres.
- [Radiology disruption] The radiology platform continues to expand despite the discontinuation of the Tamil Nadu MRI contract.

themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.
